units: <cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 44:1">Pesik. R. s. 44</cite> <he>קַבָּלַת שבים</he> the reception (in grace) of the repentant.

<cite ref="Zevachim 13a:10">Zeb. 13ᵃ</cite> <he>וק׳ מי פסלה</he> does the receiving (of the sacrificial blood by a non-priest) make the sacrifice unfit? <cite ref="Zevachim 13a:11">Ib.</cite> <he>קבלת הדם</he> receiving the blood in a vessel.
<cite ref="Mishnah Zevachim 1:4">Ib. I, 4</cite> <he>שלא בק׳</he> without the act of receiving the blood; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Gittin 62b:4">Gitt. 62ᵇ</cite> <he>שליח לק׳</he> one deputed by the woman to receive the letter of divorce in her behalf, v. <cite ref="E00237"><he>הוֹלָכָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Gittin 62b:7">Ib.</cite> <he>אק׳</he> referring to the reception of the letter of divorce in her behalf; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Metsia 5:10">Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. V, 10</cite> <he>בית ק׳</he> receptacle, v. <cite ref="S00850"><he>קִיבּוּל</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: tradition, traditional law; post-Mosaic Scriptures, opp. to תורה or תורת משה.
units: <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 7a:8">R. Hash. 7ᵃ</cite> <he>דבר זה מתורת … מדברי ק׳ למדנו</he> this (that the months are counted from Nisan) we learned not from the Law of Moses, but from the words of tradition (historical accounts, ref. to <cite ref="Zechariah 1:7">Zech. I, 7</cite>; <cite ref="Esther 2:16">Esth. II, 16</cite> &c.). Ib. 19ᵃ <he>גדליה … דברי ק׳ הוא ודברי ק׳ וכ׳</he> the account of Gedaliah, son of A., is traditional (historical, <cite ref="Jeremiah 41">Jer. XLI</cite>), and the words of tradition (post-Mosaic records) are as authoritative as the words of the Torah.
<cite ref="Chagigah 10b:10">Ḥag. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>דברי תורה מדברי ק׳ וכ׳</he> we must derive no interpretation of Mosaic laws from analogies of expression in post-Mosaic books (e.g.
<cite ref="Amos 5:25">Am. V, 25</cite> as illustrating the sense of <cite ref="Exodus 5:1">Ex. V, 1</cite>); <cite ref="Bava Kamma 2b:5">B. Kam. 2ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Niddah 23a:23">Nidd. 23ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Challah 1:1:9">Y. Ḥall. I, 57ᵇ</cite> top <he>ולמידין מן הק׳</he> can we derive a legal rule from a post-Mosaic book (<cite ref="Isaiah 28:25">Is. XXVIII, 25</cite>)?—
Gen. R. s. 7 ומן הק׳ אתה מלקני wilt thou condemn me to lashes on an inference from a post-Mosaic book?; Tanḥ. Ḥuck. 6; a. fr.—[Ber. 62ᵃ, v. קִבְלָא II.]—[In later Hebrew ק׳ Kabbalah, mystic lore.]
